0.1 This Indian Standard (First Revision) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 15 February 1978, after the draft finalized by the Pest Control Sectional Committee had bern approved by the Agricultural and Food Product! Division Council and the Chemical Divi . . ion Council.
0.2 Dichlorvos emulsifiable concentrates are largely used in the control of insects, pests and mites of agricultural importance,

0.3 Dichlorvos emulsifiable concentrate if) generully manufactured to contain 76 percent ( mlm ) of dichlorvos,
0.4 This standard was first published in 1969. Subsequently four amendments were issued. This revision incorporates the revised requrrcrnents pertaining to description, ernulvion stability, packing, cautionary notice and sampling. Opportunity has been taken to giVl� the referr-nte to IS : 6940.. ~ 973� to bring a uniform testing procedure to the various requirements In vouge,

0.5 In the preparation of this standard, due consideration has been given to the provisions l\f the Insecticides Act, 1968 and the Rules framed thereunder, However, this standard is subject to the restrictions imposed under these, wherever applicable.
0.6 For the purpoc;e of drr iding whether a particular requirement of this standard i~ complied with, the final value, observed or r alculatr-d, expressing the 1 csult of a rest r-r analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS: 2�1 ~jtiot. The number of significant places I etained in the rounded utf valaJt! should be the same as that of the specified value in this

1.1 ThiJ standard prescribes the requirements and the methods of sampling and test for dichlorvos emulsifiable concentrates. 2. REQ.UIREMENTS 2.1 Co��titueDt. - The material shall consist of dichlcrvos, technical dissolved in suitable solventjs), together with emulsifying agent(s), and with or without stabiJizer(s) and suitable dye(s). 2.1.1 Dichlorvos, technical, employed in the manufacture of this material shall conform to IS : 4929�1978-. 2.2 Phy.Jeal- The material shall comply with the physical requirements given in 2.2.1 to 2.2.... stable

2.2.1 Description - The material shall be in the form of a homogeneous liquid free from sediment. Suspended impurities shall be negligible.

2.2.2 Cold T,sl- No turbidity or separation of solid and/or oily matter shall occur when the material it subjected to the cold test at 10�C u prescribed in 13.1 of IS: 6940-1973t or any other lower temperature al agreed to between the purchaser and the vendor.

2.2.3 Flash Point ( Abel) - When determined by the method prescribed in IS: 1448 (P: 20 ]..1960:) the flash point of the material shall be above 24-5�C.
2.2.4 Emulsum SttJbililJ - Any separation, including creaming at the top and sedimentation at the bottom, of 100 ml of emulsion prepared in standard hard water with 5 ml for public health use and 2 ml for agricultural use, shall not exceed 2 ml when tested by one of the methods prescribed in 13.3 of IS : 6940-1973t.

2.3 Claemical- The material shan comply with the chemical requirement. given in 2.3.1 and 2.3.2.
